lines.text: Why does every article you read seem to prove you right?
Students for and against the death penalty read the same two studies.
One supported their view. One challenged it.
All forty-eight read identical evidence, yet each side rated the study that agreed with them as stronger.
Then both sides walked away more sure than before.
The same evidence didn't settle the debate. It split it wider.
So when something proves you right, read it twice.

post.title: Why Everything Seems to Prove You Right #shorts
post.description: Same evidence, opposite conclusions. In Lord, Ross & Lepper (1979), 48 students for and against the death penalty read the same two studies; each side rated the one that agreed with them as more convincing, and both became more sure of their view. That's confirmation bias. #psychology #cognitivebias #criticalthinking
